h1: The 5 Best Monitor Privacy Screens Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Monitor Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five monitor privacy screens, all under $50, for 24 and 27 inch displays, compared on viewing angle, coating and pack size.
summary: The Vxaop 2-pack for 27 inch monitors is the best privacy screen under $100, with a stated 60 degree viewing angle, anti-glare matte coating and 95 percent blue light reduction. The Protescreen is the other 27 inch pair, the Syhauifei 24 inch 2-pack lists exact dimensions, and the Magicmoon is aimed at open offices. The SightPro is a single 24 inch sheet.
intro: A privacy filter works only when it matches the visible dimensions of your screen, and many buyers order by the diagonal alone, then discover the film is a few millimeters off and either leaves a gap at the edge or covers the bezel. A narrow viewing angle is what makes the side view go dark, so the angle figure matters as much as the fit, and almost every cheap listing leaves it out.

This ranking weighs five filters under $100 on the Primea framework, with listed dimensions, stated viewing angle, pack size and coatings carrying the most weight. Prices appear as buckets. Four are 2-packs and one is a single sheet, and the 27 inch pair is the only choice for larger screens.

products.name: Vxaop [2-Pack] 27 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter (16:9 Aspect Ratio)
products.verdict: A 2-pack with a 60 degree viewing limit and anti-glare coating.
products.description:
This Vxaop set gives you two 27 inch filters for 16:9 monitors. The listing states 60 degree privacy protection, an anti-glare matte coating and 95 percent blue light reduction, in the $25 to $50 bucket. A 60 degree limit means the screen goes dark once someone looks from beyond that angle.

It ranks first because it publishes concrete numbers where rivals offer slogans, and a pair covers two monitors. The Protescreen is the same size and price bucket but with a thinner feature list.

Buy it for 27 inch desks needing privacy and glare control. The caveats are that it fits only 27 inch 16:9 and its dimensions are not detailed. Skip it if your monitor is not 16:9.
products.idealFor: 27 inch desks needing privacy and glare control.

It ranks second because its feature list is thinner than the Vxaop, with no stated viewing angle. Both are 27 inch pairs at the same price, so the Vxaop's published figures decide it.

products.name: [2-Pack] 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen 16:9 Aspect Ratio Widescreen Monitor

It ranks third because the listed dimensions let you measure against your screen before buying, which no other listing offers as clearly. The viewing angle is not stated, though.

Buy it for two 24 inch monitors with a measured fit. The caveats are the unlisted angle and the need to check fit first. Skip it if you do not want to measure first.

It ranks fourth because the listing gives few numbers and no exact dimensions, so you must trust the diagonal. It matches the Syhauifei on pack size.

It ranks last because you get one filter, not two, so a dual-monitor desk costs more. It lists dimensions, which helps the fit, but gives no pack savings.

Buy it for one 24 inch monitor. The caveats are the single filter and no pack savings. Skip it if you have two monitors.

whatMatters.detail: Privacy filters are cut to the visible screen area, not the diagonal alone. A few millimeters off leaves a gap or covers the bezel. Measure your visible area and compare it to the listing, such as 532 by 299 mm, and treat a diagonal-only listing as a risk. Measure the lit area of the panel, not the outer bezel, and write the numbers down.

The viewing angle is how far from center the screen stays readable. A narrower angle like 60 degrees blocks more side views. Look for a stated figure, and be cautious when a listing says only that the screen looks dark from the side, because the angle is the measure. A narrower angle protects more but also narrows your own comfortable seating position.

Most listings are for 16:9 monitors. An ultrawide or 16:10 panel will not fit. Check your monitor's ratio first in the spec sheet or settings, and measure the visible width and height, because the same diagonal can come in different shapes. Divide width by height to confirm 16:9.

Anti-glare and blue light features add comfort. They matter if you work long hours. Look for a matte coating or a blue light percentage, as on the Vxaop, and note that these add a little tint and reduce brightness. Colour-critical work suffers most, so skip the blue light option if accuracy matters.

Some filters use adhesive strips, others tabs. Removable options help if you share the screen. Check the mounting description, and avoid adhesives on a screen you plan to resell or share often. Tabs and clips let you swap the film between screens.

faq.q: Will a 24 inch filter fit any 24 inch monitor?
faq.a: Only if the visible area matches. The Syhauifei and SightPro list 532 by 299 mm, so measure first. Two 24 inch monitors can differ by several millimeters, and a film that is too large will not sit flat.
No, these are for 16:9 monitors. Ultrawide panels need a different cut, and a 16:10 screen will leave a gap along the edge. Check your ratio before you spend.

faq.q: Is the Vxaop worth it over the Protescreen?
faq.a: It lists a 60 degree angle, anti-glare and blue light numbers, while the Protescreen does not. Both are 27 inch 2-packs in the same price bucket, so the published figures are the tiebreaker.

faq.q: How do I install a filter?
faq.a: Clean the screen and attach using the included mounting method. The Syhauifei lists two methods. Dust under the film shows as bright spots, so wipe the glass carefully first and work in a clean room.

Privacy films usually darken the picture somewhat. Raise brightness if needed, and expect a little loss of sharpness, which is the price of the side-view block. The anti-glare coatings reduce reflections in return.
Removable mounts allow this, and tab systems are easier to take off than adhesive strips. Check the mounting description before buying if you plan to share the screen or sell the monitor later.

finalTake: Buy the Vxaop for 27 inch monitors, since it publishes the most numbers. The Syhauifei suits two 24 inch screens when you have measured the visible area, and the Magicmoon suits shared offices. Take the SightPro only for a single monitor. Measure your visible area before you order.
